name: Heat Stroke
overview: Working long hours in the sun can lead to heat exhaustion or heat stroke. Heat stroke is a medical emergency.

steps.title: Move to shade or indoors
steps.detail: Get the person out of the sun and into a cooler place.

steps.title: Cool the body
steps.detail: Remove excess clothing. Apply cool, wet cloths to skin. Fan them. If possible, immerse in cool (not cold) water.

steps.title: Hydrate if alert
steps.detail: If the person is conscious and can swallow, give small sips of water. Do not give alcohol or caffeine.

steps.title: Monitor
steps.detail: Watch for vomiting, seizures, or loss of consciousness.

when_to_seek_help: Call 911 if: hot, dry skin and no sweating; confusion or slurred speech; seizures; loss of consciousness; temperature over 103°F. Heat stroke can cause brain damage or death if not treated quickly.
prevention_tips: Drink water often; don't wait until thirsty.
Take breaks in the shade every 1–2 hours.
Wear a hat and light-colored, loose clothing.
Work during cooler parts of the day when possible.
